workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/prototype-specs is a small Playwright project that drove the Design Release 2.1 traces (trace:prototype-dr2-1) against the GB-notification-service prototype mounted at /design-release-2.1. In scope: the 10 fit specs in e2e/ (99 test() calls by grep, 103 tests reported by COVERAGE.md, about 2,620 lines): about-the-consignment (351 lines, 20 tests: notification type, origin, what are you importing, main import reason, germinal section 1), description-of-the-goods (249, 7), transport-and-arrival (272, 10), documents (124, 7), consignment-parties (398, 14: role pickers, add-address, permanent address, contact address), journeys (391, 5 plus the hub/review/declaration tests), dashboard (213, 8), manage-notifications (195, 7: view, amend, cancel-amend, copy, delete), templates (206, 12) and address-book (220, 9); the shared helper e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines: page actions and shared assertions every spec calls); and COVERAGE.md (201 lines: the route table of 67 routes with visiting tests and captured states, the 36 DR2.1 override views, what was not reached and why, and 15 behaviours worth knowing). Plumbing read for context only: README.md, e2e/support/fixtures.js and evidence.js, playwright.config.js. Left out: explore/ (ad hoc exploration scripts and their ~180 text dumps, which are not the driving suite; their findings that matter are restated in COVERAGE.md), the run/collect/coverage scripts and package files. Cut by feature area, one or two spec files per part following the journey order, with COVERAGE.md as its own part; every spec part reads journey.js in full but claims only the assertions its own tests make.

Extracted in 7 parts:
Part 1, Section 1: type, origin, commodity, reason: Part 1 read e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js (351 lines) and e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines) in full. The spec has four describe blocks plus one germinal block, 20 tests in all, following DR2.1 task-list section 1 (About the consignment) under /design-release-2.1: 'notification type' (3 tests: /create-notification redirects to /notification-type with five type options, its required error, draft reference GBN-AG-26-..., a /live-animals dashboard 'Create new' that skips the type question, and plants for planting reaching an empty commodity search); 'origin of the import' (4 tests: title, heading, caption, country search placeholder, region of origin code Yes/No with hint, revealed code input with country prefix and 'Enter up to 5 characters.', empty-code error, internal reference field and hint, no hub button or cancel link, country optional, answers kept, country search pick); 'what are you importing' (5 tests: ITAHC copy, search label and hint, two action buttons, cancel link to /notification-hub, commodity code help and Trade Tariff link, 'Select a commodity' error, species search with result count and Latin-name checkboxes, selection panel with count, groups, per-species remove and Clear all, hub save without validating); 'main import reason' (7 tests: five reasons with hints, reason optional, internal market with 11 purposes and its required error, transhipment destination country, transit port of exit and destination country, temporary admission horses exit date and port of exit with real-date error, the /prototype/reason-for-import seed route); 'germinal products: section 1' (1 test: ?category=germinal-products start, back link to /germinal-products, germinal search hint and 'semen' results, reasons reduced to Internal market and Transit, purposes reduced to four). journey.js supplies the shared assertions these tests make (error summary title and linked messages, inline errors, back links, draft reference, action button values, the type-and-pick autocomplete, commodity selection hidden value, MOJ date picker input, species fixtures, the /design-release-2.1 mount); its later helpers (arrival, documents, addresses, transporter, consignment details) belong to other parts and are not claimed here. Claims keep the ids of the earlier part 1 extract: the spec and helper are unchanged since it, and every claim was re-checked against them. Gaps recorded: Potatoes and Wood products types, plants after the commodity page, hub save keeping a selection, Re-entry's reveal, and where a complete temporary admission answer leads.
Part 2, Goods, transport and arrival, documents: Part 2 of 7 (Goods, transport and arrival, documents). Read in full: e2e/description-of-the-goods.fit.spec.js (249 lines; 3 describe blocks, 7 tests: commodity details x3 for cattle, two commodities and germinal products; identification details x2 for cattle and germinal products; additional details x2 for cattle and poultry), e2e/transport-and-arrival.fit.spec.js (272 lines; 4 describe blocks, 10 tests: arrival details x2, transit countries x1, transporter details x3 including the legacy /transport-details redirect, add a transporter x4 for type choice, private add, private cancel and commercial add), e2e/documents.fit.spec.js (124 lines; 2 describe blocks, 7 tests: upload documents x6 and upload documents from the hub x1), and the shared helper e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines; the /design-release-2.1 base path, error summary, inline error and back link assertions, the action button group, the bespoke autocompletes, the MOJ date picker, species fixtures and the per-page answer helpers). Claims cover the pages /consignment-details (Commodity details), /animal-identification-details (Identification details), /additional-animal-details (Additional details), /arrival-details, /transit-countries, /transporter, /transport-details (legacy redirect), /transporter/add, /transporter/add/private, /transporter/add/commercial and /upload-documents (including ?from=hub): each page's title, heading, caption, body copy, fields, options, hints, error messages in order, conditional reveals, branches, redirects and back links, as each test asserts them. journey.js is shared by every part; only the conventions these pages use and the helpers for these pages are claimed here. Refs are spec file, line and test name. Gaps record what the pages show but no test proves.
Part 3, Consignment parties and contact address: Part 3 read e2e/consignment-parties.fit.spec.js (398 lines) and e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines) in full. The spec has 14 tests in four describe blocks: 'consignment addresses' (7: cattle five roles plus CPH, cat permanent address replacing CPH, picking every role then the CPH number, same-as shortcuts, picker search, continue with nothing chosen, save and return to hub), 'add an address from the journey' (2: place of origin international by hand, consignee UK lookup), 'add-address pages for the other roles' (1: consignor, importer, place of destination), 'permanent address' (2: per-animal choice and its errors, retired enter-address redirect) and 'contact address for consignment' (2: choice and error, add a new branch address). A shared toRoles helper starts a live-animals notification, answers origin, commodity (cattle x1 or cat x2), reason and consignment details, then goes to /roles-and-addresses by URL. Pages covered, all under /design-release-2.1: /roles-and-addresses, the five pickers (/place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination), their /add-address pages, /cph-number, /permanent-address, /permanent-address/select, /permanent-address/enter-address, /contact-address-for-consignment, with exits to /notification-hub, /review-notification and /address-book/add/lookup. From journey.js only the helpers these tests call are claimed: the base path, the action button values, the error summary title, the CORE_ADDRESSES fixture ids, chooseAddress, fillCph and answerContactAddress. Claims p3-001 to p3-110 keep the ids of an earlier extract of this same slice (the spec is unchanged since); p3-111 to p3-113 are new.
Part 4, End-to-end journeys, hub, review and declaration: Part 4 read in full e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js (391 lines) and the shared helper e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines). journeys.fit.spec.js has two describe blocks. 'notification journeys end to end' runs one test per entry of JOURNEYS (5 tests: cattle by air, poultry by rail, pet cats by air, horse by sea, germinal bovine semen), each driven by walk() (notification type or category, origin, what are you importing, main import reason, commodity details, optional identification details, optional additional details, arrival details, optional transit countries, transporter, upload documents, roles and addresses with optional CPH and permanent address, contact address) then reviewAndSubmit() (hub shows every task Complete, review your notification, declaration with its empty-submit error, notification submitted, the submitted notification viewed by reference). 'the notification hub' has 4 tests: a fresh notification lists every task as to do, a hub task link returns to the hub after saving, review with tasks missing lists each incomplete section, and the submitted page is guarded until the declaration is confirmed. journey.js supplies the mount (/design-release-2.1), the page actions every step calls (field names, ids, button values) and the shared assertions (error summary title, back link, heading, reference format); only what these 9 tests drive or assert is claimed here. Claims are ordered: shared walk steps, the hub after completion, review, declaration, submitted page, view after submit, one claim per journey's distinguishing route and review content, then the four hub tests, then gaps.
Part 5, Dashboards and managing notifications: Part 5 of 7, Dashboards and managing notifications. Read in full: e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js (213 lines; 3 describe blocks, 8 tests: overall dashboard (summary cards, /dashboard redirects, the prototype index), category dashboards (live animals with tabs, search, sort and additional filters; germinal products with packages), and the three at-a-glance drill-downs /actions, /changes and /inspection); e2e/manage-notifications.fit.spec.js (195 lines; 5 describe blocks, 7 tests: view a notification per status (submitted action required, submitted, completed, draft), amend a submitted notification (confirm modal, change and save and return, held continue, valid arrival, declaration and resubmit), cancel an amendment, amend and copy guards, copy as new, delete with confirmation and banner); e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines; shared helpers: the /design-release-2.1 mirror mount, url helpers, action-button values, date format, autocomplete and journey steps). Claims cover every route, title, heading, caption, tab, column text, status tag, filter, link target, button, modal, banner and redirect these tests assert, plus gaps where a test title promises more than its assertions prove. From journey.js only what the dashboards and manage-notification flows rely on is claimed (mount, action button values, date format, reference format, create-new redirect); the journey-step helpers belong to other parts' journeys.
Part 6, Templates and address book: Part 6, Templates and address book. Read in full: e2e/templates.fit.spec.js (206 lines, 12 tests in three describe blocks: 'manage templates' 2 tests — the list and the dashboard Use template button; 'a saved template' 6 tests — view, use, change one section, POST reload plus unknown template, edit on its own task list, delete; 'create a new template' 4 tests — type then name then answers then review and save, Untitled template, discard, discard outside a template journey), e2e/address-book.fit.spec.js (220 lines, 9 tests in three describe blocks: 'address book list' 1 multi-step test — default category, page 2, the three other categories, search inside the Filter addresses disclosure; 'add an address to the address book' 6 tests — choose an address type with its error, origin or consignor by hand with errors and uses, destination/consignee/importer by search with errors and uses, branch use, transporter hand-off, the usage step guard; 'an address book entry' 2 tests — view/edit/save with error and banner, delete with banner) and the shared helper e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines: the /design-release-2.1 mount, url/urlFor, the action-button and submit helpers, expectHeading, expectErrorSummary with its 'There is a problem' title, expectBackLink, answerOrigin and answerCommodity used by the template-creation test). Every path below is under the /design-release-2.1 mount. Claims cover each route, title, heading, caption, label, hint, option, error message verbatim, banner, back link, redirect and count the 21 tests assert; journey.js is claimed only where these two specs call it. Gaps record what the tests leave unasserted (template-name validation, the address usage step with an address pending, add-address success banner, the address view page's delete link, button text on the review and edit forms).
Part 7, COVERAGE.md: Part 7, COVERAGE.md. Read in full: COVERAGE.md (201 lines), plus README.md, e2e/support/fixtures.js and e2e/support/evidence.js for context. COVERAGE.md has an intro (prototype pulled from main on 7 October 2026, 103 tests all passing, the route table generated from the trace and evidence indexes, 'Visited by' counting redirect hops), then four sections. Routes: a generated table between routes:start and routes:end of 65 GET routes under /design-release-2.1 (not 67 as the partition expected), each with the view it renders (DR2.1 override, shared root view, or redirect), how many tests visit it with one example test name, and the evidence states captured; claimed one route per claim (p7-001 to p7-065), with the example test names that state a behaviour claimed separately (p7-176 to p7-208). DR2.1 override views: 36 rows, one per file in app/views/design-release-2.1/, with the routes that render each and whether it is visited; all are visited except permanent-address, which is unreachable; claimed p7-066 to p7-101. Not reached, and why: 5 items (permanent-address override, the virus-check JSON endpoint, the address-book usage page, dashboard pagination and filter results, POST /intro/sign-in), split into p7-109 to p7-118. Behaviour worth knowing: 15 numbered items, each split into one claim per fact (p7-119 to p7-175); the two facts in item 6 that COVERAGE.md marks observed in exploration but not asserted are inferred. README and the support plumbing add how traces record every main-frame request including redirect hops, and that each evidence state is owned by the first test to reach it (p7-205, p7-206); the README's arrival-date window is cited alongside item 11 (p7-161).
